text:
alex: Quick heads-up — in the nightly perf run I saw KV prefix cache hit rate drop ~18% when increasing batch size from 64 -> 256 for the 13B model. Latency mostly stayed within SLO but token cost jumped. Anyone available to run a focused hotspot scan + flamegraph? I pushed the raw run to perf: http://perf.rw/bench/17699

maya: Can you paste the hit rate numbers and the sequence-length distribution? If p95 seq len moved that's an easy explanation.

alex: Hit rate numbers: 0.87 @ b=64 -> 0.71 @ b=256. Seq len p95 went from 62 -> 140 (weird). Quick log snippet from the run:
```
KV_HIT=0.87
KV_HIT=0.71
KV_EVICT_RATE=0.009 -> 0.024
```

sam: I can trigger a profiler. Plan: run bench with kv-profiling + heatmap across batch sizes and collect flamegraphs. Command I'll use:
```
/run-bench --model=redwood/13b --batch-sizes=64,128,256 --seq-dist=observed --profile=kv,flame --warmup=500
```
I'll queue it now.

ci-bot: Job queued: bench-176990_run1 — ETA ~25m. Artifacts will be on CI when complete: https://ci.redwood/bench/176990_run1

devon: Also check kv_fragmentation_ratio, we've seen fragmentation grow after the LRU tweak from two weeks ago. Metric to watch: 
```
sum(kv_fragmentation_bytes) / sum(kv_allocated_bytes)
```
If fragmentation > 0.15 that's suspicious.

linh: I'll run a targeted test with fixed seq len 64 vs fixed 128 to isolate whether seq-length skew is the root cause. Will post eviction heatmaps and traces.

alex: Also pinging @maya @sam for a quick CR on PR 3421 — the LRU change that landed ~2 weeks ago. Suspect it nudged eviction ordering. PR: https://git.redwood/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3421

maya: I can review tonight. Leave a short checklist of hotspots to focus on (kv eviction code paths, bucket balancing).

sam: Another thing to correlate: we shipped q4_ssr quant variant in the same window. That changes per-shard memory layout and could increase fragmentation. Worth checking memory footprint per-variant.

ops-bot: alert: kv-evict-rate spike detected in region us-west-2 at 2026-03-14T03:12:47Z — auto-notifying #incidents if sustained.

devon: If we need to bisect, recommend warmup-only bisect across commits 8f3a..b912 with minimal workload (fast to run).

alex: Thanks all. @linh @sam please post bench links + flamegraphs when available. If fragmentation looks like the root cause we should prepare an LRU rollback plan and an A/B run.

maya: :thumbsup: will do a first-pass review and flag anything obvious.

ci-bot: bench-176990_run1 completed: artifacts https://ci.redwood/artifacts/176990_run1 (flamegraphs + kv-stats).
